q21035.en: When you meet the traffic light shown, you may pass when the green light is on.

explain.short: Green means you may go through, if the road ahead is free.
explain.rule: Vehicle lights: green = go. Steady yellow = stop, unless you are too close to stop safely. Red = stop before the line. Flashing yellow, or a light that is off or broken = go slowly, with great care, and give way as the priority rules say.
explain.trap: No trick: 'luce verde' (green light) is the normal 'go' light.

sceneParams.caption: Green light: you may pass

q21036.en: When you meet the traffic light shown, you may pass when the steady yellow light comes on, only if you cannot stop safely before the junction.

explain.short: Steady yellow means stop. You may go on only when you are so close that braking would be dangerous.
explain.rule: Vehicle lights: green = go. Steady yellow = stop, unless you are too close to stop safely. Red = stop before the line. Flashing yellow, or a light that is off or broken = go slowly, with great care, and give way as the priority rules say.
explain.trap: 'solo se non ci si può arrestare' (only if you cannot stop) is the correct exception.

sceneParams.caption: Steady yellow: go on only if too close to stop
lines: Too close to stop safely? Go on

keywords.it: solo se non ci si può arrestare

q21037.en: When you meet the traffic light shown, you may pass when the flashing yellow light is on, but with the greatest care and at a moderate speed.

explain.short: Flashing yellow does not stop you: it warns you. Slow down, look, and follow the priority rules.
explain.rule: Vehicle lights: green = go. Steady yellow = stop, unless you are too close to stop safely. Red = stop before the line. Flashing yellow, or a light that is off or broken = go slowly, with great care, and give way as the priority rules say.
explain.trap: 'lampeggiante' (flashing) is not 'fissa' (steady): flashing yellow lets you pass with care.

sceneParams.caption: Flashing yellow: pass slowly, with care
lines: Flashing yellow: pass with great care
Slow down, give way as needed

q21038.en: When you meet the traffic light shown, you may pass when it is switched off, but with the greatest care.

explain.short: A light that is off gives no order. You may pass, but slowly, following the normal priority rules and signs.
explain.rule: Vehicle lights: green = go. Steady yellow = stop, unless you are too close to stop safely. Red = stop before the line. Flashing yellow, or a light that is off or broken = go slowly, with great care, and give way as the priority rules say.
explain.trap: 'spento' (off) does not mean stop: you go on with the greatest care.

sceneParams.caption: Light off: pass with the greatest care
lines: Light off: no order from the light
Pass with care, normal priority rules

q21039.en: When you meet the light signal shown, you may pass if the traffic light is broken, but with the greatest care.

explain.short: A broken light cannot control traffic. You may pass, slowly, following the priority rules.
explain.rule: Vehicle lights: green = go. Steady yellow = stop, unless you are too close to stop safely. Red = stop before the line. Flashing yellow, or a light that is off or broken = go slowly, with great care, and give way as the priority rules say.
explain.trap: 'guasto' (broken) is treated like a light that is off: pass with care.

sceneParams.caption: Broken light: pass with the greatest care
lines: Broken light: pass with great care

q21040.en: When you meet the traffic light shown, you may pass shortly before the green light comes on, as long as the red light is already on for the other vehicles.

explain.short: While your light is red you must wait. You start only when your own light is green.
explain.rule: Vehicle lights: green = go. Steady yellow = stop, unless you are too close to stop safely. Red = stop before the line. Flashing yellow, or a light that is off or broken = go slowly, with great care, and give way as the priority rules say.
explain.trap: 'poco prima che si accenda la luce verde' (just before green) is still red for you: you wait.

sceneParams.caption: Not before your green: red still means stop
lines: Your light is still red: wait
Go only when YOUR light is green

keywords.it: quella rossa per gli altri veicoli
keywords.en: the red one for the other vehicles

q21041.en: When you meet the traffic light shown, you may pass when the red light comes on, using the greatest care.

explain.short: Red always means stop before the stop line. Being careful does not make it allowed.
explain.rule: Vehicle lights: green = go. Steady yellow = stop, unless you are too close to stop safely. Red = stop before the line. Flashing yellow, or a light that is off or broken = go slowly, with great care, and give way as the priority rules say.
explain.trap: 'usando la massima prudenza' (with great care) cannot cancel a red light.

sceneParams.caption: Red: stop. Care does not make it allowed
lines: Being careful does not change it

q21042.en: When you meet the traffic light shown, you may pass when, even though the red light is on, no vehicles are coming from the other directions.

explain.short: Red means stop even if the junction looks empty. You wait for green.
explain.rule: Vehicle lights: green = go. Steady yellow = stop, unless you are too close to stop safely. Red = stop before the line. Flashing yellow, or a light that is off or broken = go slowly, with great care, and give way as the priority rules say.
explain.trap: 'pur essendo accesa la luce rossa' (even though it is red): an empty road does not change the rule.

sceneParams.caption: Red: stop even if nobody is coming
lines: Even if the junction is empty

keywords.it: pur essendo accesa la luce rossa
keywords.en: even though the red light is on

q21043.en: The lights shown can be found near level crossings with half-barriers.

explain.short: Flashing red lights stand at level crossings with half-barriers (semibarriere): they warn that the barriers are about to come down.
explain.rule: Two red lights that flash alternately stand at level crossings (passaggi a livello) with half-barriers (semibarriere) or without barriers, normally on the right of the road. They switch on just before the train comes and before the half-barriers go down, with a sound signal, and stay on until the train has passed. When they flash, vehicles and pedestrians must stop.
explain.trap: 'semibarriere' (half-barriers) is right: these lights go with them.

sceneParams.caption: Found at level crossings with half-barriers

q21044.en: The lights shown light up alternately to signal that trains are coming at level crossings without barriers.

explain.short: Where there are no barriers, these alternately flashing red lights are the warning that a train is coming.
explain.rule: Two red lights that flash alternately stand at level crossings (passaggi a livello) with half-barriers (semibarriere) or without barriers, normally on the right of the road. They switch on just before the train comes and before the half-barriers go down, with a sound signal, and stay on until the train has passed. When they flash, vehicles and pedestrians must stop.
explain.trap: 'alternativamente' (alternately) is right: left and right flash in turn.

sceneParams.caption: No barriers: flashing lights warn of the train
lines: No barriers: lights warn of the train

q21045.en: The lights shown, when they are on, forbid vehicles and pedestrians to pass.

explain.short: When these red lights flash, nobody may cross the railway: not cars, not pedestrians.
explain.rule: Two red lights that flash alternately stand at level crossings (passaggi a livello) with half-barriers (semibarriere) or without barriers, normally on the right of the road. They switch on just before the train comes and before the half-barriers go down, with a sound signal, and stay on until the train has passed. When they flash, vehicles and pedestrians must stop.
explain.trap: 'veicoli e pedoni' (vehicles and pedestrians): the stop is for everyone.

sceneParams.caption: Lights on: vehicles and pedestrians stop

q21046.en: The lights shown are, as a rule, placed on the right side of the road.

explain.short: Like most signals, these lights normally stand on the right side of the road, where drivers see them.
explain.rule: Two red lights that flash alternately stand at level crossings (passaggi a livello) with half-barriers (semibarriere) or without barriers, normally on the right of the road. They switch on just before the train comes and before the half-barriers go down, with a sound signal, and stay on until the train has passed. When they flash, vehicles and pedestrians must stop.
explain.trap: 'di norma' (as a rule): normally on the right, sometimes repeated elsewhere.

sceneParams.caption: As a rule: on the right side of the road
lines: Normally on the right of the road

q21047.en: The lights shown start working shortly before the train arrives and stay on until it has finished passing.

explain.short: The lights come on a little before the train and go off only when the train has gone by.
explain.rule: Two red lights that flash alternately stand at level crossings (passaggi a livello) with half-barriers (semibarriere) or without barriers, normally on the right of the road. They switch on just before the train comes and before the half-barriers go down, with a sound signal, and stay on until the train has passed. When they flash, vehicles and pedestrians must stop.
explain.trap: 'fino alla fine del suo passaggio' (until it has passed): not off earlier.

sceneParams.caption: On before the train, off after it has passed
lines: Off: only after the train has passed

keywords.it: fino alla fine del suo passaggio

q21048.en: The lights shown come on just before the half-barriers start to go down.

explain.short: First the red lights start flashing, then the half-barriers come down. The lights warn you in time.
explain.rule: Two red lights that flash alternately stand at level crossings (passaggi a livello) with half-barriers (semibarriere) or without barriers, normally on the right of the road. They switch on just before the train comes and before the half-barriers go down, with a sound signal, and stay on until the train has passed. When they flash, vehicles and pedestrians must stop.
explain.trap: 'subito prima' (just before) is right: lights first, barriers second.

sceneParams.caption: Lights first, then barriers come down

q21049.en: The lights shown work together with a sound signal device.

explain.short: With the flashing lights there is also a sound (a bell or buzzer), so you notice the danger even without looking.
explain.rule: Two red lights that flash alternately stand at level crossings (passaggi a livello) with half-barriers (semibarriere) or without barriers, normally on the right of the road. They switch on just before the train comes and before the half-barriers go down, with a sound signal, and stay on until the train has passed. When they flash, vehicles and pedestrians must stop.
explain.trap: 'segnalazione acustica' (sound signal) is right: you see AND hear the warning.

sceneParams.caption: Lights plus a sound signal

q21050.en: When approaching a level crossing with red lights flashing alternately and the half-barrier still up, you must get ready to stop.

explain.short: The flashing lights mean a train is coming and the barrier is about to go down. Slow down and prepare to stop.
explain.rule: Two red lights that flash alternately stand at level crossings (passaggi a livello) with half-barriers (semibarriere) or without barriers, normally on the right of the road. They switch on just before the train comes and before the half-barriers go down, with a sound signal, and stay on until the train has passed. When they flash, vehicles and pedestrians must stop.
explain.trap: 'ancora alzata' (still up): the open barrier does not mean you can go.

sceneParams.caption: Barrier still up but lights flash: get ready to stop
lines: Slow down, get ready to stop

q21051.en: When approaching a level crossing with red lights flashing alternately and the half-barrier still up, you may pass quickly if you do not see any train coming.

explain.short: Flashing red lights mean stop, even if the barrier is still up and you cannot see the train yet. Trains are fast and need a long way to brake.
explain.rule: Two red lights that flash alternately stand at level crossings (passaggi a livello) with half-barriers (semibarriere) or without barriers, normally on the right of the road. They switch on just before the train comes and before the half-barriers go down, with a sound signal, and stay on until the train has passed. When they flash, vehicles and pedestrians must stop.
explain.trap: 'se non si vede sopraggiungere alcun treno' (if you see no train): the lights count, not your eyes.

sceneParams.caption: Never rush across: flashing red means stop
lines: Even if you cannot see a train

q21052.en: The lights shown are found along railway lines, as a traffic light for train drivers.

explain.short: These lights face the road: they are for drivers and pedestrians crossing the railway, not for train drivers.
explain.rule: Two red lights that flash alternately stand at level crossings (passaggi a livello) with half-barriers (semibarriere) or without barriers, normally on the right of the road. They switch on just before the train comes and before the half-barriers go down, with a sound signal, and stay on until the train has passed. When they flash, vehicles and pedestrians must stop.
explain.trap: 'per i conducenti dei treni' (for train drivers) is wrong: they are for road users.

sceneParams.caption: For road users at the crossing, not for trains
lines: For cars and pedestrians at the crossing
Not a signal for train drivers

q21053.en: The lights shown, when they flash alternately, invite you to occupy the level crossing quickly.

explain.short: Flashing red lights mean the opposite: stop, do not go onto the crossing.
explain.rule: Two red lights that flash alternately stand at level crossings (passaggi a livello) with half-barriers (semibarriere) or without barriers, normally on the right of the road. They switch on just before the train comes and before the half-barriers go down, with a sound signal, and stay on until the train has passed. When they flash, vehicles and pedestrians must stop.
explain.trap: 'invitano a occupare rapidamente' (invite you to hurry onto it) is the opposite of the real meaning.

sceneParams.caption: Flashing red: stop, do not hurry across
lines: Flashing red: stop before the crossing

q21054.en: The lights shown can be found 150 metres before a level crossing with barriers.

explain.short: These lights stand at the crossing itself, not 150 m before. 150 m before there is a danger sign instead.
explain.rule: Two red lights that flash alternately stand at level crossings (passaggi a livello) with half-barriers (semibarriere) or without barriers, normally on the right of the road. They switch on just before the train comes and before the half-barriers go down, with a sound signal, and stay on until the train has passed. When they flash, vehicles and pedestrians must stop.
explain.trap: '150 metri prima' (150 m before) is wrong: the lights are right at the crossing.

sceneParams.caption: At the crossing itself, not 150 m before
lines: The lights are AT the crossing

q21055.en: The lights shown are placed on the first of the distance panels of a level crossing.

explain.short: The distance panels (pannelli distanziometrici) have red stripes, no lights. The flashing lights are at the crossing.
explain.rule: Two red lights that flash alternately stand at level crossings (passaggi a livello) with half-barriers (semibarriere) or without barriers, normally on the right of the road. They switch on just before the train comes and before the half-barriers go down, with a sound signal, and stay on until the train has passed. When they flash, vehicles and pedestrians must stop.
explain.trap: 'pannelli distanziometrici' (distance panels) are striped boards before the crossing, not where the lights go.

sceneParams.caption: Lights at the crossing, not on the distance panels
lines: Distance panels: red stripes, no lights
The lights stand at the crossing

q21056.en: The light device shown is made of alternately flashing lights that come on while the half-barriers are opening (going up).

explain.short: The lights come on before the half-barriers go DOWN, not when they go up. When the barriers go up, the train has passed.
explain.rule: Two red lights that flash alternately stand at level crossings (passaggi a livello) with half-barriers (semibarriere) or without barriers, normally on the right of the road. They switch on just before the train comes and before the half-barriers go down, with a sound signal, and stay on until the train has passed. When they flash, vehicles and pedestrians must stop.
explain.trap: 'fase di apertura (sollevamento)' (opening, going up) is wrong: they come on before the lowering.

sceneParams.caption: They come on before the barriers go DOWN
lines: Lights on: barriers about to go down
Barriers go up: train has passed

q21057.en: The light signals shown are traffic lights for reversible lanes.

explain.short: Lights hung above each lane, with a red X and arrows, control reversible lanes (corsie reversibili).
explain.rule: Lights over the lanes for reversible lanes (corsie reversibili: lanes whose direction can change). Red X = you must not use that lane. Green arrow pointing down = you may use that lane. Flashing yellow arrow = move into the lane the arrow points to. They apply to all vehicles, bicycles too, not to pedestrians.
explain.trap: 'corsie reversibili' (reversible lanes) is right: lanes whose direction can change.

sceneParams.caption: Lights for reversible lanes

q21058.en: The traffic light shown does not let you occupy the lane marked with a red X-shaped light.

explain.short: A red X over a lane means that lane is closed to you: do not drive in it.
explain.rule: Lights over the lanes for reversible lanes (corsie reversibili: lanes whose direction can change). Red X = you must not use that lane. Green arrow pointing down = you may use that lane. Flashing yellow arrow = move into the lane the arrow points to. They apply to all vehicles, bicycles too, not to pedestrians.
explain.trap: 'non consente' (does not allow) is right for the red X.

sceneParams.caption: Red X: do not use that lane
lines: Red X: lane closed to you

keywords.en: does not allow you to occupy

q21059.en: The traffic light shown lets you enter the lane shown by the green arrow.

explain.short: A green arrow pointing down over a lane means that lane is open to you.
explain.rule: Lights over the lanes for reversible lanes (corsie reversibili: lanes whose direction can change). Red X = you must not use that lane. Green arrow pointing down = you may use that lane. Flashing yellow arrow = move into the lane the arrow points to. They apply to all vehicles, bicycles too, not to pedestrians.
explain.trap: 'impegnare' (enter / use) is right with the green arrow.

sceneParams.caption: Green arrow: you may use that lane
lines: Green arrow: lane open to you

q21060.en: In the traffic lights shown, the flashing yellow light obliges the driver to move into the lane shown by the arrow.

explain.short: The flashing yellow slanted arrow tells you to leave your lane and move to the one it points to.
explain.rule: Lights over the lanes for reversible lanes (corsie reversibili: lanes whose direction can change). Red X = you must not use that lane. Green arrow pointing down = you may use that lane. Flashing yellow arrow = move into the lane the arrow points to. They apply to all vehicles, bicycles too, not to pedestrians.
explain.trap: 'obbliga' (obliges) is right: it is an order to change lane.

sceneParams.caption: Flashing yellow arrow: move to that lane
lines: Move into the lane it points to

q21061.en: The traffic light shown does not let you occupy the lanes shown by the green arrows.

explain.short: Green arrows mean the opposite: those lanes are open to you.
explain.rule: Lights over the lanes for reversible lanes (corsie reversibili: lanes whose direction can change). Red X = you must not use that lane. Green arrow pointing down = you may use that lane. Flashing yellow arrow = move into the lane the arrow points to. They apply to all vehicles, bicycles too, not to pedestrians.
explain.trap: 'non consente' (does not allow) is wrong for green: only the red X closes a lane.

sceneParams.caption: Green arrow lanes are OPEN to you
lines: Green arrow: you may use the lane
Only the red X closes it

keywords.en: does not allow you to occupy

q21062.en: The traffic light shown also applies to pedestrians.

explain.short: These lights are over the lanes of the carriageway: they are for vehicles. Pedestrians have their own lights.
explain.rule: Lights over the lanes for reversible lanes (corsie reversibili: lanes whose direction can change). Red X = you must not use that lane. Green arrow pointing down = you may use that lane. Flashing yellow arrow = move into the lane the arrow points to. They apply to all vehicles, bicycles too, not to pedestrians.
explain.trap: 'anche per i pedoni' (also for pedestrians) is wrong: vehicles only.

sceneParams.caption: For vehicles in the lanes, not pedestrians

q21063.en: In the traffic lights shown, the red X-shaped light orders you to stop and wait for the yellow light.

explain.short: The red X does not mean 'stop and wait': it means you must not drive in that lane. Use an open lane.
explain.rule: Lights over the lanes for reversible lanes (corsie reversibili: lanes whose direction can change). Red X = you must not use that lane. Green arrow pointing down = you may use that lane. Flashing yellow arrow = move into the lane the arrow points to. They apply to all vehicles, bicycles too, not to pedestrians.
explain.trap: 'arrestarsi ed attendere la luce gialla' (stop and wait for yellow) is invented.

sceneParams.caption: Red X: lane closed, not 'wait for yellow'
lines: Red X: do not use this lane
Use a lane with a green arrow

q21064.en: The traffic light shown does not apply to bicycles.

explain.short: Bicycles are vehicles: lane lights apply to them too.
explain.rule: Lights over the lanes for reversible lanes (corsie reversibili: lanes whose direction can change). Red X = you must not use that lane. Green arrow pointing down = you may use that lane. Flashing yellow arrow = move into the lane the arrow points to. They apply to all vehicles, bicycles too, not to pedestrians.
explain.trap: 'non vale per le biciclette' (not for bicycles) is wrong: bikes must obey too.

sceneParams.caption: Bicycles must obey these lights too

q21065.en: The green light on in the traffic light shown lets pedestrians cross.

explain.short: This is a pedestrian traffic light: the green little person means pedestrians may cross.
explain.rule: A light with a little person is a pedestrian traffic light. Green: pedestrians may step onto the road and cross. Yellow: do not start crossing. Red: do not cross. Turning vehicles must give way to pedestrians crossing on green. It has nothing to do with lifts, escalators or schools.
explain.trap: 'pedoni' (pedestrians) is right: the figure is a person on foot.

sceneParams.caption: Green pedestrian light: you may cross

q21066.en: The green light on in the traffic light shown allows pedestrians to cross the road.

explain.short: Green on the pedestrian light: people on foot may cross the road.
explain.rule: A light with a little person is a pedestrian traffic light. Green: pedestrians may step onto the road and cross. Yellow: do not start crossing. Red: do not cross. Turning vehicles must give way to pedestrians crossing on green. It has nothing to do with lifts, escalators or schools.
explain.trap: 'attraversare la strada' (cross the road) is right with the green person.

sceneParams.caption: Green person: cross the road

q21067.en: The green light on in the traffic light shown allows pedestrians to step onto the carriageway to cross it.

explain.short: With the green person, pedestrians may step onto the carriageway (carreggiata: the part of the road for vehicles) and cross it.
explain.rule: A light with a little person is a pedestrian traffic light. Green: pedestrians may step onto the road and cross. Yellow: do not start crossing. Red: do not cross. Turning vehicles must give way to pedestrians crossing on green. It has nothing to do with lifts, escalators or schools.
explain.trap: 'impegnare la carreggiata' (step onto the carriageway) is right: that is how you cross.

sceneParams.caption: Green person: step onto the road and cross
lines: Green person: step onto the road

q21068.en: The traffic light shown indicates an escalator in operation.

explain.short: The little person shows a pedestrian traffic light, not an escalator.
explain.rule: A light with a little person is a pedestrian traffic light. Green: pedestrians may step onto the road and cross. Yellow: do not start crossing. Red: do not cross. Turning vehicles must give way to pedestrians crossing on green. It has nothing to do with lifts, escalators or schools.
explain.trap: 'scala mobile' (escalator) is an invented meaning.

sceneParams.caption: A pedestrian light, not an escalator

q21069.en: The green light on in the traffic light shown lets only vehicles pass.

explain.short: The little person shows it is for pedestrians, not for vehicles.
explain.rule: A light with a little person is a pedestrian traffic light. Green: pedestrians may step onto the road and cross. Yellow: do not start crossing. Red: do not cross. Turning vehicles must give way to pedestrians crossing on green. It has nothing to do with lifts, escalators or schools.
explain.trap: 'solo dei veicoli' (only vehicles) is wrong: it is for people on foot.

sceneParams.caption: For pedestrians, not only vehicles

q21070.en: The green light on in the traffic light shown obliges pedestrians to give way to vehicles that are turning.

explain.short: It is the other way round: turning vehicles must give way to pedestrians crossing on green.
explain.rule: A light with a little person is a pedestrian traffic light. Green: pedestrians may step onto the road and cross. Yellow: do not start crossing. Red: do not cross. Turning vehicles must give way to pedestrians crossing on green. It has nothing to do with lifts, escalators or schools.
explain.trap: 'obbliga i pedoni a dare la precedenza' (pedestrians must give way) swaps the roles.

sceneParams.caption: Turning cars give way to pedestrians
lines: Turning vehicles give way to them

q21071.en: The traffic light shown indicates a public lift.

explain.short: The little person shows a pedestrian traffic light, not a lift.
explain.rule: A light with a little person is a pedestrian traffic light. Green: pedestrians may step onto the road and cross. Yellow: do not start crossing. Red: do not cross. Turning vehicles must give way to pedestrians crossing on green. It has nothing to do with lifts, escalators or schools.
explain.trap: 'ascensore pubblico' (public lift) is an invented meaning.

sceneParams.caption: A pedestrian light, not a lift

q21072.en: The traffic light shown signals a primary school, so you must slow down.

explain.short: A school is shown by a danger sign (triangle with children), not by this pedestrian light.
explain.rule: A light with a little person is a pedestrian traffic light. Green: pedestrians may step onto the road and cross. Yellow: do not start crossing. Red: do not cross. Turning vehicles must give way to pedestrians crossing on green. It has nothing to do with lifts, escalators or schools.
explain.trap: 'scuola elementare' (primary school) is wrong: this is a pedestrian light.

sceneParams.caption: A pedestrian light, not a school sign
lines: Pedestrian light, not a school sign

q21073.en: The green light of the traffic light shown is always on while students are leaving school.

explain.short: A pedestrian light works in normal cycles. There is no rule that it stays green when pupils leave school.
explain.rule: A light with a little person is a pedestrian traffic light. Green: pedestrians may step onto the road and cross. Yellow: do not start crossing. Red: do not cross. Turning vehicles must give way to pedestrians crossing on green. It has nothing to do with lifts, escalators or schools.
explain.trap: 'sempre accesa' (always on) is invented.

sceneParams.caption: Normal cycle, not always green at school time

q21074.en: The light signal shown is a traffic light for vehicles.

explain.short: Three round lights, red, yellow and green, with no symbols: this is the normal light for vehicles.
explain.rule: The three-light traffic light (red, yellow, green) is for vehicles, bicycles and buses included. It normally stands at a junction (incrocio) to control who passes. Steady yellow: stop, but if you are already in the junction, clear it. Flashing yellow: you may pass with care.
explain.trap: 'per i veicoli' (for vehicles) is right: plain round lights.

sceneParams.caption: Normal traffic light for vehicles

q21075.en: The traffic light shown is, as a rule, placed at a junction.

explain.short: Traffic lights are normally at junctions (incroci), where traffic from different roads meets.
explain.rule: The three-light traffic light (red, yellow, green) is for vehicles, bicycles and buses included. It normally stands at a junction (incrocio) to control who passes. Steady yellow: stop, but if you are already in the junction, clear it. Flashing yellow: you may pass with care.
explain.trap: 'di norma' (as a rule): mostly at junctions, sometimes also at pedestrian crossings.

sceneParams.caption: As a rule: at a junction

q21076.en: The traffic light shown is used, as a rule, to control the passage of vehicles at a junction.

explain.short: Its job is to decide who passes at a junction, by turns.
explain.rule: The three-light traffic light (red, yellow, green) is for vehicles, bicycles and buses included. It normally stands at a junction (incrocio) to control who passes. Steady yellow: stop, but if you are already in the junction, clear it. Flashing yellow: you may pass with care.
explain.trap: 'regolare il passaggio' (control the passage) is right.

sceneParams.caption: It controls who passes at the junction

q21077.en: The traffic light shown, with the steady yellow light on, lets you cross the junction if you have already entered it.

explain.short: If yellow comes on when you are already inside the junction, you must clear it: go on and leave it free.
explain.rule: The three-light traffic light (red, yellow, green) is for vehicles, bicycles and buses included. It normally stands at a junction (incrocio) to control who passes. Steady yellow: stop, but if you are already in the junction, clear it. Flashing yellow: you may pass with care.
explain.trap: 'se lo si è già impegnato' (if you are already in it) is the key condition.

sceneParams.caption: Yellow but already inside: clear the junction
lines: Steady yellow: stop if you can
Already in the junction? Clear it

q21078.en: The traffic light shown does not apply to public passenger transport vehicles.

explain.short: Buses obey normal traffic lights too. Only on some reserved lanes do they have special lights.
explain.rule: The three-light traffic light (red, yellow, green) is for vehicles, bicycles and buses included. It normally stands at a junction (incrocio) to control who passes. Steady yellow: stop, but if you are already in the junction, clear it. Flashing yellow: you may pass with care.
explain.trap: 'non vale' (does not apply) is wrong: the normal light is for all vehicles.

sceneParams.caption: Buses obey this light too

q21079.en: The light signal shown is a traffic light that does not apply to bicycles.

explain.short: Bicycles are vehicles: they must obey the normal traffic light.
explain.rule: The three-light traffic light (red, yellow, green) is for vehicles, bicycles and buses included. It normally stands at a junction (incrocio) to control who passes. Steady yellow: stop, but if you are already in the junction, clear it. Flashing yellow: you may pass with care.
explain.trap: 'non vale per le biciclette' (not for bicycles) is wrong.

sceneParams.caption: Bicycles obey this light too

q21080.en: The traffic light shown is found at all motorway toll booths.

explain.short: This light is normally at junctions. Toll booths (caselli) do not all have it.
explain.rule: The three-light traffic light (red, yellow, green) is for vehicles, bicycles and buses included. It normally stands at a junction (incrocio) to control who passes. Steady yellow: stop, but if you are already in the junction, clear it. Flashing yellow: you may pass with care.
explain.trap: 'tutti' (all) is the trap word: there is no such rule.

sceneParams.caption: Normally at junctions, not at every toll booth

q21081.en: The traffic light shown is found near railway tracks.

explain.short: Near railway tracks you find the two red flashing lights of level crossings, not this three-light signal.
explain.rule: The three-light traffic light (red, yellow, green) is for vehicles, bicycles and buses included. It normally stands at a junction (incrocio) to control who passes. Steady yellow: stop, but if you are already in the junction, clear it. Flashing yellow: you may pass with care.
explain.trap: 'binari ferroviari' (railway tracks) is wrong: this light is for junctions.

sceneParams.caption: For junctions, not railway tracks
lines: Junction light, not a railway light

q21082.en: The traffic light shown, with the flashing yellow light on, does not allow vehicles to pass.

explain.short: Flashing yellow allows you to pass, slowly and carefully, giving way as the rules say.
explain.rule: The three-light traffic light (red, yellow, green) is for vehicles, bicycles and buses included. It normally stands at a junction (incrocio) to control who passes. Steady yellow: stop, but if you are already in the junction, clear it. Flashing yellow: you may pass with care.
explain.trap: 'non consente il transito' (does not allow passing) is wrong: flashing yellow is not red.

sceneParams.caption: Flashing yellow: you may pass with care

q21083.en: The light signals shown are lane traffic lights.

explain.short: Lights with arrows are lane traffic lights (semafori di corsia): each one is for one direction.
explain.rule: Lights with arrows are lane traffic lights (semafori di corsia). Each one is for vehicles going in the direction of its arrow. Green arrow = go, only that way. Steady yellow arrow = stop, or clear the junction at once if you are already in it. Red arrow = stop. Off = go with special care. They apply to all vehicles, bicycles too.
explain.trap: 'semafori di corsia' (lane traffic lights) is right: arrows instead of round lights.

sceneParams.caption: Arrow lights = lane traffic lights

q21084.en: The traffic light shown concerns vehicles that must go on in the direction of the arrow.

explain.short: Each arrow light is only for the vehicles going the way it points.
explain.rule: Lights with arrows are lane traffic lights (semafori di corsia). Each one is for vehicles going in the direction of its arrow. Green arrow = go, only that way. Steady yellow arrow = stop, or clear the junction at once if you are already in it. Red arrow = stop. Off = go with special care. They apply to all vehicles, bicycles too.
explain.trap: 'nella direzione della freccia' (in the arrow's direction) is right.

sceneParams.caption: Each light is for its arrow's direction
lines: Arrow light: only for that direction

q21085.en: The traffic light shown lets you go on only in the direction of the green arrow.

explain.short: The green arrow lets you go only the way it points, not in other directions.
explain.rule: Lights with arrows are lane traffic lights (semafori di corsia). Each one is for vehicles going in the direction of its arrow. Green arrow = go, only that way. Steady yellow arrow = stop, or clear the junction at once if you are already in it. Red arrow = stop. Off = go with special care. They apply to all vehicles, bicycles too.
explain.trap: 'sola' (only) is right: other directions follow their own light.

sceneParams.caption: Green arrow: go only that way
lines: Green arrow: go only that way

q21086.en: The traffic lights shown, if switched off, let you pass with particular care.

explain.short: Lights that are off give no order: you may pass, carefully, following the priority rules.
explain.rule: Lights with arrows are lane traffic lights (semafori di corsia). Each one is for vehicles going in the direction of its arrow. Green arrow = go, only that way. Steady yellow arrow = stop, or clear the junction at once if you are already in it. Red arrow = stop. Off = go with special care. They apply to all vehicles, bicycles too.
explain.trap: 'se spenti' (if off) does not mean stop: pass with care.

sceneParams.caption: Lights off: pass with particular care

q21087.en: The lane traffic lights shown, with the red arrow on, order vehicles going in the arrow's direction to stop.

explain.short: A red arrow stops only the vehicles going that way.
explain.rule: Lights with arrows are lane traffic lights (semafori di corsia). Each one is for vehicles going in the direction of its arrow. Green arrow = go, only that way. Steady yellow arrow = stop, or clear the junction at once if you are already in it. Red arrow = stop. Off = go with special care. They apply to all vehicles, bicycles too.
explain.trap: 'diretti nel senso della freccia' (going the arrow's way): only they must stop.

sceneParams.caption: Red arrow: stop if you go that way
lines: Only if you go that way

q21088.en: The traffic lights shown, with the steady yellow arrow on, order you to clear the junction at once if you have already entered it.

explain.short: Steady yellow arrow: if you are already in the junction, leave it quickly so it is free for others.
explain.rule: Lights with arrows are lane traffic lights (semafori di corsia). Each one is for vehicles going in the direction of its arrow. Green arrow = go, only that way. Steady yellow arrow = stop, or clear the junction at once if you are already in it. Red arrow = stop. Off = go with special care. They apply to all vehicles, bicycles too.
explain.trap: 'liberare immediatamente' (clear at once) is right when you are already inside.

sceneParams.caption: Yellow arrow, already inside: clear it at once

q21089.en: The light signals shown also apply to bicycles.

explain.short: Bicycles are vehicles, so they obey lane traffic lights too.
explain.rule: Lights with arrows are lane traffic lights (semafori di corsia). Each one is for vehicles going in the direction of its arrow. Green arrow = go, only that way. Steady yellow arrow = stop, or clear the junction at once if you are already in it. Red arrow = stop. Off = go with special care. They apply to all vehicles, bicycles too.
explain.trap: 'anche' (also) is right: bikes are included.

sceneParams.caption: Bicycles obey lane lights too
lines: Bicycles are vehicles: they obey too

q21090.en: The light signals shown are traffic lights for public passenger transport vehicles.

explain.short: Arrow lights are for all vehicles going that way, not only for buses.
explain.rule: Lights with arrows are lane traffic lights (semafori di corsia). Each one is for vehicles going in the direction of its arrow. Green arrow = go, only that way. Steady yellow arrow = stop, or clear the junction at once if you are already in it. Red arrow = stop. Off = go with special care. They apply to all vehicles, bicycles too.
explain.trap: 'in servizio di linea' (public line service) is wrong: they are for everybody.

sceneParams.caption: For all vehicles, not only buses

q21091.en: The light signals shown are traffic lights for rail vehicles (trams, trains).

explain.short: Trams and trains have their own special lights. These coloured arrows are lane lights for road vehicles.
explain.rule: Lights with arrows are lane traffic lights (semafori di corsia). Each one is for vehicles going in the direction of its arrow. Green arrow = go, only that way. Steady yellow arrow = stop, or clear the junction at once if you are already in it. Red arrow = stop. Off = go with special care. They apply to all vehicles, bicycles too.
explain.trap: 'veicoli su rotaie' (rail vehicles) is wrong.

sceneParams.caption: For road vehicles, not trams or trains
lines: Trams and trains have other lights

q21092.en: The light signals shown are placed at the start of a tunnel.

explain.short: Lane lights are used at junctions to control each direction, not at tunnel entrances.
explain.rule: Lights with arrows are lane traffic lights (semafori di corsia). Each one is for vehicles going in the direction of its arrow. Green arrow = go, only that way. Steady yellow arrow = stop, or clear the junction at once if you are already in it. Red arrow = stop. Off = go with special care. They apply to all vehicles, bicycles too.
explain.trap: 'galleria' (tunnel) is a wrong place.

sceneParams.caption: At junctions, not at tunnel entrances

q21093.en: The traffic lights shown are used at the entrances to lifting bridges.

explain.short: Lane lights with arrows control directions at junctions, not access to lifting bridges.
explain.rule: Lights with arrows are lane traffic lights (semafori di corsia). Each one is for vehicles going in the direction of its arrow. Green arrow = go, only that way. Steady yellow arrow = stop, or clear the junction at once if you are already in it. Red arrow = stop. Off = go with special care. They apply to all vehicles, bicycles too.
explain.trap: 'ponti mobili' (lifting bridges) is a wrong place.

sceneParams.caption: At junctions, not at lifting bridges

q21094.en: The traffic lights shown control the entrance to the boarding pier of ferry boats.

explain.short: Lane lights control directions at junctions, not boarding onto ferries.
explain.rule: Lights with arrows are lane traffic lights (semafori di corsia). Each one is for vehicles going in the direction of its arrow. Green arrow = go, only that way. Steady yellow arrow = stop, or clear the junction at once if you are already in it. Red arrow = stop. Off = go with special care. They apply to all vehicles, bicycles too.
explain.trap: 'navi traghetto' (ferry boats) is a wrong place.

sceneParams.caption: At junctions, not at ferry piers

q21095.en: The traffic lights shown control crossing a level crossing.

explain.short: Level crossings use two red lights flashing alternately, not arrow lights.
explain.rule: Lights with arrows are lane traffic lights (semafori di corsia). Each one is for vehicles going in the direction of its arrow. Green arrow = go, only that way. Steady yellow arrow = stop, or clear the junction at once if you are already in it. Red arrow = stop. Off = go with special care. They apply to all vehicles, bicycles too.
explain.trap: 'passaggio a livello' (level crossing) is wrong for arrow lights.

sceneParams.caption: Level crossings use flashing red lights
lines: Level crossing: two flashing red lights

q21096.en: The light signals shown are traffic lights for reversible lanes.

explain.short: Reversible-lane lights hang over the lanes and use a red X and a green downward arrow. These are lane lights for directions at a junction.
explain.rule: Lights with arrows are lane traffic lights (semafori di corsia). Each one is for vehicles going in the direction of its arrow. Green arrow = go, only that way. Steady yellow arrow = stop, or clear the junction at once if you are already in it. Red arrow = stop. Off = go with special care. They apply to all vehicles, bicycles too.
explain.trap: 'corsie reversibili' (reversible lanes) is wrong: those lights have a red X.

sceneParams.caption: Lane lights, not reversible-lane lights
lines: Reversible lanes: red X, green arrow
